title: The Effects of Oral Contraceptives on Exercise Performance in Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
claims: The review included 42 studies and 590 participants.
Most studies (83%) were graded as moderate, low or very low quality, and 17% achieved high quality.
Oral contraceptive use might result in slightly inferior exercise performance on average compared with naturally menstruating women, but any group-level effect is most likely trivial.

The probability of a small effect favouring naturally menstruating women was moderate to small depending on the comparison method, and the probability of an effect favouring oral contraceptive users was effectively zero.
Exercise performance appeared relatively consistent across the oral contraceptive cycle, so different guidance for pill-taking versus non-pill-taking days is not warranted.
The authors conclude that current evidence does not support general guidance on oral contraceptive use versus non-use for performance.
